subject: Does knownOcc change detection and occupancy estimations for models?

messages.author: 1cad400e913f30eb
messages.subject: Does knownOcc change detection and occupancy estimations for models?
parts:
What does knownOcc do when applied to single season occupancy models?  Does it result in different estimates for occupancy probabilities? I understand how known occupancy for sites can be added to the model, but it is not clear to me what it actually does in the implementation of calculations and how it might effect resulting estimates.

Thanks,
Nick Smeenk

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Does knownOcc change detection and occupancy estimations for models?
parts:
hi Nick,
 if you specify knownOcc for some sites then it changes the likelihood for those sites to include only detection parameters (normally when occupancy status is not known a priori then the likelihood for the data from a given site includes both p and psi parameters). In general you would expect this to influence both detection and occupancy estimates, but the difference should be small when you have a decent sample size.  To be honest I can't remember where this is discussed explicitly in the literature. 
regards,
andy
